case_description: Someone stole my mobile phone from my pocket in a crowded bus.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek legal guidance on the following incident:

On [date] at approximately [time], I was a passenger on a crowded public bus (as defined under Article 2(12) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) when my personal mobile phone was allegedly stolen from my person by an unknown individual. I intend to seek compensation and restitution for the loss under Article 35(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

I request clarification on the burden of proof to establish the identity of the perpetrator, the admissibility of circumstantial evidence under Article 27(3) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, and the applicable provisions for reporting and investigating this incident under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the procedural requirements for filing a complaint under Article 22(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 and the rights and obligations of the investigating authority in this matter.

case_description: A man entered my house at night by breaking the door and took my jewelry.
rephrased_query:
Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I wish to seek clarification on the applicability of Article 321 (Criminal Trespass) and Article 322 (Theft), in relation to the alleged offence committed by an individual who forcibly entered my residential premises at night, thereby causing damage to my property, and subsequently, stealing my jewelry. 

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I would like to know the procedures for reporting the incident, obtaining a First Information Report (FIR), and subsequent investigation. 

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I wish to inquire about the admissibility of evidence and any specific provisions related to the collection, preservation, and presentation of physical evidence (such as the broken door and stolen jewelry) that may be relevant to the case.

case_description: My neighbor keeps threatening to beat me if I use the common parking area.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 113 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek guidance on whether my neighbor's verbal statements constitute an offense under the rubric of "criminal intimidation" as defined in the BNS, specifically in relation to Section 1(1) of Article 113. Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request clarification on the necessary prerequisites for filing a complaint against my neighbor, as per Article 27, BNSS, in order to prevent the alleged threat of physical harm and ensure my safety. 

Furthermore, I wish to inquire about the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in establishing the prima facie case, specifically regarding Article 11, BSA, which pertains to the relevance and materiality of witness statements in support of my complaint.

case_description: Two people started fighting on the street and one hit the other with a stick causing injuries.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the applicability of the provisions concerning the infliction of bodily harm.

A case of intentional harm is alleged to have been committed by an individual, who struck another person with a stick, resulting in physical injuries. The circumstances of the incident necessitate an examination of Article 324 of the BNS, which defines the offense of voluntarily causing hurt.

Specifically, I request an interpretation of the elements required to be established for guilt, as stipulated under Article 324, and the corresponding punishment prescribed thereunder, in conjunction with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding the procedure for investigating and prosecuting such offenses.

Additionally, the admissibility of evidence collected from the scene of the incident, as well as any statements made by the parties involved, may be subject to the provisions of Article 207 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) concerning the relevance and reliability of testimony and documentary evidence.

case_description: A person sent me abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically against the offence of 'Intentional Public Mischief' (Section 494(1)(a) of BNS) and 'Harassment through Electronic Means' (Section 523(e) of BNS), where the accused person has been sending abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp to the complainant, thereby causing mental distress and harassment. 

Further, it may be pertinent to enquire whether the complainant's fundamental right to privacy has been violated under the BNS, specifically Section 217(2)(c), and whether the accused's actions constitute a cognizable offence as defined under Section 3(2) of the BNSS, warranting investigation and arrest under Section 19(1)(d) of the BNSS.

Additionally, it would be relevant to seek proof of the accused's identity and the transmission of the messages through electronic evidence under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Section 35(1)(b) and Section 46(3)(d), to establish the prima facie case against the accused.

case_description: Someone forged my signature on a cheque and withdrew money from my account.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek a clarification on the applicability of the offence of forgery under Section 16(B)(i) of the BNS to the alleged act of forging my signature on a cheque, thereby causing an unauthorized withdrawal of funds from my account. 

Furthermore, I request guidance on the procedures to be followed under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 in order to file a complaint and initiate an investigation in this matter, specifically with regard to the duties of the police officer under Section 27 of the BNSS, and the requirements for producing evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

case_description: My landlord locked me out of my rented room without any notice and kept my belongings inside.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek legal advice on whether the actions of my landlord constitute the offence of "House Trespass" under Section 17(1)(a) of BNS, and further, if such actions amount to "Theft by Person Having Special Care and Trust" under Section 25(1) of BNS.

Furthermore, under the framework of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request clarification on the procedure to be followed to obtain relief and compensation under Section 46(2) of BNSS for the alleged wrongful act, and to determine whether a Magistrate's Order under Section 19(1) of BNSS is necessary to restore my possession of the rented room and recover my belongings.

Additionally, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to prove the aforementioned allegations, particularly with respect to the burden of proof and the standard of evidence required to establish the commission of these offences.

case_description: A group of people damaged my shop during a protest by throwing stones and breaking the glass.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we respectfully submit the following incident report:

Whether, under Article 123 of the BNS, the perpetrators of the aforementioned incident can be held liable for the destruction of private property, specifically the damage to the complainant's shop, as a result of their intentional and unlawful act of throwing stones and breaking glass, thereby causing harm to the property and disrupting public order?

Further, we seek to determine whether the actions of the perpetrators constitute a cognizable offence under Chapter IV of the BNS, warranting immediate arrest and investigation, and whether the provisions of Section 12 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding the registration of FIRs and the powers of the police to investigate and gather evidence will be applicable in this instance.

Additionally, we request clarification on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) regarding the testimony of witnesses, including whether the provisions of Article 45 of the BSA regarding the reliability of witness statements in the presence of other corroborating evidence will be relevant in this case.

case_description: A stranger keeps calling and sending messages threatening to burn my shop if I do not pay him money.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Protection from Harassment and Economic Extortion: 

Respected Magistrate, under Article 294(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit a complaint against an unknown individual who has been persistently harassing me through telephonic calls and text messages, threatening to inflict property damage to my shop if I fail to comply with his unlawful demand for pecuniary compensation.

Pursuant to Article 12 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the Magistrate take cognizance of this complaint and direct the concerned authorities to register an FIR under the relevant provisions of BNS, and to take necessary measures to protect me from further intimidation and economic coercion.

I humbly request the Magistrate to direct the investigating officer to gather evidence, including but not limited to, the records of the threatening calls and messages, to establish the identity of the perpetrator and to take action against him in accordance with law.

In view of Article 53 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request that the Magistrate direct the investigating officer to preserve all evidence related to this case and to produce the same before the court during the pendency of the investigation.

case_description: Someone hacked my social media account and posted offensive content using my name.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I submit the following formal complaint:

Whether Section 44 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 ("Mischievous intent" causing harm to reputation) has been violated, in view of the hacking of my social media account and the posting of offensive content using my name, thereby causing harm to my reputation (as per Article 123(1)(a)(ii) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023)? 

Under Section 13 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I request an investigation into this incident and the prosecution of the perpetrator(s) under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, as applicable.

Further, I request guidance on the admissibility of evidence under Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically with regard to the digital footprint and other relevant records that may be obtainable in this case.

case_description: During a land dispute my uncle stabbed my father multiple times with a knife and he died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the offence committed by my uncle, wherein he inflicted grievous injuries upon my father, resulting in his instantaneous demise. 

Specifically, I wish to know whether my uncle's actions amount to an offence under Article 302 of the BNS, which pertains to murder, and whether this constitutes an instance of culpable homicide not amounting to murder as defined under Article 304 of the BNS.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request guidance on the procedure for filing a complaint and the subsequent investigation to be conducted by the authorities in this matter.

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek clarification on the admissibility of the available evidence, including eyewitness testimony and forensic reports, as per the principles of admissibility under Article 63 of the BSA and the burden of proof as per Article 74 of the BSA.

case_description: A man poured acid on a woman's face after she rejected his marriage proposal and she later succumbed to injuries.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek an interpretation on the following scenario:

Whether the act of a male individual, who intentionally causes harm to a female person by pouring acid on her face, amounts to the offense of "Grihapatya Aparadh" under Article 302 of the BNS, specifically when such act was committed as a retaliatory measure following the female person's rejection of the male individual's proposal for marriage? Further, whether the subsequent death of the female person due to injuries sustained from the acid attack, would constitute a separate offense under the BNS.

Additionally, we seek guidance on the applicability of the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Section 173(8), which deals with the circumstances under which a Magistrate may take cognizance of a non-cognizable offense, in the present scenario.

Lastly, we wish to enquire about the admissibility of certain statements made by the accused to a police officer, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly Section 23(3), which deals with the circumstances under which a statement made by an accused person may be considered as a relevant fact.

case_description: My neighbor hit my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument; he is in ICU and may not survive.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Registration of FIR under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and subsequent investigation under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) 

Is the incident on hand a case of "Voluntary causing grievous hurt" punishable under Section Article 325(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, as allegedly committed by the neighbor, resulting in severe injuries to the victim (petitioner's brother) who is admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and is at risk of dying as a direct consequence of the said injuries, thereby attracting the provisions of Article 304 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and necessitating a thorough investigation under Chapter VI of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to gather evidence under the provisions of Chapter III of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023?

Further, what are the admissibility and weightage of various types of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, especially in cases where the alleged perpetrator attempts to deny or mislead the investigation under the provisions of Article 117 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023?

case_description: Two men got into a drunken fight and one pushed the other off a bridge, causing his death.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Section 302 is hereby invoked. 

 Query: 
In the circumstances where two male individuals engaged in a physical altercation while under the influence of intoxicating substances, resulting in one of them being forcibly propelled off a bridge, leading to his demise, what constitutes the applicable provision(s) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and what is the corresponding penalty under the said law?

Furthermore, under the aegis of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Section 173(8) is pertinent to the facts of this case.

Query:
What is the procedure to be followed by the law enforcement agencies in collecting and preserving physical evidence at the scene of the crime, and what are the requirements for the prompt and diligent investigation of this incident as stipulated under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)?

Lastly, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) is relevant to the admissibility of the evidence collected in this case.

Query:
What are the criteria for the admissibility of the physical evidence, including eyewitness testimony, medical records, and any other relevant documents, as provided under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA)?

case_description: A bus driver was driving recklessly at high speed and ran over a pedestrian who died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Whether the bus driver commits the offence of 'reckless endangerment of life or personal safety of others' under Article 174 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and whether the provisions of Section 176 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding 'accidental death' and the corresponding procedures for investigation and prosecution under Article 123 of the BNS are applicable in this case.

Furthermore, what is the admissibility of evidence in this case under the provisions of Chapter 5 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Section 45, which deals with the testimony of eyewitnesses, and can the prosecution rely on the statements of bystanders and other witnesses under the provisions of Article 76 of the BSA?

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Section 498A, it is submitted for consideration that the deceased, a married woman, was subjected to cruel treatment by her husband and in-laws, resulting in the demand for dowry in contravention of Article 15 of the Prohibition of Dowry Demands Act, 1961.

Further, it is alleged that the aforesaid cruel treatment culminated in the deceased's untimely demise by hanging within two years of her marriage, which appears to be a case of dowry-related death as defined under Article 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Kindly consider taking cognizance of this matter under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Article 173, to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deceased's death and to determine the culpability of the perpetrators.

In this regard, it would be beneficial to examine the evidence collected, including the statements of witnesses, medical reports, and other relevant documents, in light of the principles laid down in Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), Article 59, to ascertain the facts of the case and to ensure that justice is served.

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS):

Whether the defendant, a minor, can be held liable under Article 39 of BNS for abetment of suicide, punishable under Article 43, in relation to the deceased classmate, in view of the defendant's online communication encouraging the deceased to end her life, which led to the deceased's eventual demise?

Pursuant to Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), this complaint may be registered under BNSS Article 190, wherein the police are empowered to investigate and file a chargesheet under Article 191, if sufficient evidence is found to establish the commission of the said offense.

Request for the investigation to be guided by the principles of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 27, which deals with the admissibility of electronic evidence, including social media posts and online communications, in the trial of the offense.

case_description: A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to clarify the applicability of Section 302 of BNS, relating to punishment for murder, to the accused, who is a life-convict on parole, in light of Section 8 of BNS, which pertains to the revocation of parole in the event of a breach of parole conditions.

Moreover, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the following questions arise:

- What are the procedures for apprehending and detaining the accused, as outlined in Section 57 of BNSS?
- What are the provisions for filing a police report and initiating an investigation, as set forth in Article 23 of BNSS?
- What are the procedures for conducting the investigation, as specified in Section 41 of BNSS?

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the following queries pertain:

- What are the admissibility and reliability criteria for evidence collected during the investigation, as per Section 35 of BSA?
- What are the procedures for the examination and cross-examination of witnesses, as outlined in Article 27 of BSA?

Please provide the relevant information regarding these matters.

case_description: A man fired his licensed gun at his business partner during a heated dispute but the bullet missed narrowly.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Inquiry under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023:

Whether the act of the accused, who allegedly fired a licensed firearm at his business partner during a heated dispute, constitutes an offence under Article 37 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 ("Discharge of Arms or Ammunition in Violation of Law") and/or Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 ("Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder")?

Petition for Inquiry under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023:

Is the accused liable to be arrested and detained under Article 27 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 ("Police Inquiry and Arrest") for the alleged offence, and if so, what is the appropriate procedure for the arrest and subsequent custodial interrogation of the accused?

Petition for Evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023:

What evidence, if any, is required to be adduced by the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 ("Burden of Proof") in relation to the alleged offence, and what is the standard of proof required to be met by the prosecution in this regard?

case_description: A cook mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and three guests died after consuming it.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Prosecution (Section 302 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023): 

Whether the acts of the cook, who intentionally mixed rat poison into the food served at a party, resulting in the deaths of three guests, constitute the offence of murder as defined under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and whether the cook can be held liable for the said offence under Section 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Also, a petition to invoke the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023:

Pursuant to Article 53 of the BNSS, whether a Magistrate should take cognizance of the offence and direct the police to register an FIR under Section 154 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and whether the Magistrate should exercise jurisdiction under Article 55 of BNSS to authorise the police to investigate the case.

Additionally, a query under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023:

Whether the circumstantial evidence collected from the party premises, including food samples and witness statements, can be admissible as evidence under Section 6 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, and whether the prosecution can rely on such evidence to prove the guilt of the accused under Section 8 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

case_description: My 8-year-old son was taken away by unknown persons from outside his school and we received a ransom call demanding ten lakh rupees.
rephrased_query:
Petition under Section 82 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), seeking registration of a First Information Report (FIR) based on an alleged kidnapping and extortion, as follows:

To the Magistrate/Police Officer as per Section 4(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

Subject: Reporting of Cognizable Offence under Section 3(1) of the BNS.

An incident has allegedly occurred where a minor child, namely [son's name], aged 8 years, was taken away by unknown persons from outside his school, and subsequently, a ransom call was received demanding a sum of ten lakh rupees. We request registration of a First Information Report and investigation into this matter under Section 4(2) of the BNSS.

We request the Magistrate/Police Officer to consider the following facts and circumstances of the case:

- Date and time of incident: [Insert date and time]
- Place of incident: [Insert location, i.e., outside the school]
- Description of the kidnapped child: [Insert details of the child]
- Description of the ransom call: [Insert details of the ransom call]

We request that the necessary steps be taken to ensure the safe return of the kidnapped child and to apprehend the perpetrators of this crime, as per Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.

We request that this petition be treated as a complaint under Section 2(1) of the BNSS and that the necessary action be taken in accordance with law.

Please find attached the supporting documents, including a medical certificate and any other relevant evidence, as per Section 59 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

Signed,

[Your Name]

case_description: A young woman was lured with a fake job offer and trafficked to another state where she was forced into prostitution.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the act of inducing a young woman with a false promise of employment constitutes an offence under Article 17(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and whether such conduct, coupled with the subsequent transportation to another state, could be classified as an instance of 'forced servitude' under Article 19(7) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiaya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the procedural steps and jurisdictional requirements for registering a complaint and initiating an investigation into this incident?

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the admissibility of digital evidence, such as online communications and social media records, as proof of the alleged offence, particularly in establishing the intent and knowledge of the accused?

case_description: A gang kidnapped children from railway stations and maimed them to use for organized begging.
rephrased_query:
Petition to invoke provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against perpetrators of organised begging and infliction of grievous bodily harm on minors.

Whether the acts of kidnapping and maiming of children by a gang, with the intention of using them for organised begging, amount to an offence under Article 321(1) of BNS, specifically Article 321(1) (a) (i) (iii) which pertains to 'kidnapping' and/or Article 321(1) (b) (i) (ii) which pertains to 'voluntarily causing grievous hurt', in conjunction with Article 321(2) (a) which prescribes punishment for 'gang' activity?

Further, whether the provisions of Article 456 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding 'search and seizure' can be invoked to gather evidence against the accused, and whether the safeguards enshrined under Article 456(2) have been complied with?

Moreover, in the event of prosecution under Article 321 of BNS, whether the burden of proof under Article 789 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) would shift to the accused to prove their innocence, and whether the accused can be held liable for the offence under Article 321(3) (a) which prescribes the principle of 'collective guilt'?

case_description: My teenage daughter was taken away by a man she met online without my knowledge or consent.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit a request for legal assistance in the following matter:

Is the act of a person, a minor's acquaintance met online (hereinafter referred to as 'the perpetrator'), who forcibly or deceitfully removes and secludes the minor (my daughter) from the lawful custody of her parent (myself) without the latter's knowledge, consent, or permission, punishable under BNS Article 322(1) ('Unlawful restraint'), Article 353 ('Kidnapping from lawful guardianship'), or Article 365 ('Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty')?

Further, I request clarification on the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) that govern the reporting, investigation, and prosecution of such incidents, specifically BNSS Chapter VIII ('Cognizance of Offences by Magistrates') and BNSS Chapter X ('Police Investigation'). 

Lastly, I seek guidance on the admissibility of digital evidence, as per Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), in establishing the guilt of the perpetrator, particularly in the context of BSA Article 34 ('Relevant facts' including 'digital communications') and BSA Article 45 ('Primary evidence').

case_description: An auto-rickshaw driver forcibly took a woman passenger to an isolated area against her will.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is being lodged against the auto-rickshaw driver for alleged commission of the offence under Section 354A(1)(i) of BNS, which pertains to the act of 'unwanted physical contact or advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures' or 'making physical contact without the consent of the woman'. 

It is further alleged that the accused auto-rickshaw driver committed an act under Section 294 of BNS, which pertains to the 'outraging the modesty of a woman by any act of physical intrusion.' It is also alleged that the accused auto-rickshaw driver committed the offence under Section 365 of BNS, which pertains to kidnapping or abducting with intent to compel for unlawful marriage, or to extort ransom or other valuable thing, or with intent to subject her to grievous hurt, slavery, etc.

Further, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a First Information Report (FIR) is being sought to be registered against the accused auto-rickshaw driver for these alleged crimes.

Moreover, pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the complainant requests that the court direct the police to record the statement of the complainant under Section 161 of BSA, as an eyewitness to the alleged offence, and also to record the statement of any other relevant witnesses under Section 164 of BSA.

The complainant requests that the court grants necessary protection to the complainant under Section 83 of BNSS and to any other relevant witnesses under Section 109 of BNSS.

case_description: A child under ten was stolen from her parents at a mela and later found being sold to a couple in another city.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek guidance on the following matter:

Whether the act of removing a minor child (under the age of ten) from her lawful guardians (her parents) at a mela, with the intention of permanently depriving them of their custody, constitutes an offence under Article 123(1) of the BNS, which pertains to "Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder" or Article 123(2), which pertains to "Culpable Homicide amounting to Murder" or Article 124, which pertains to "Dowry Death" or Article 125, which pertains to "Causing death of a child under twelve years of age by an act amounting to culpable homicide".

Furthermore, we seek clarification on the applicability of the provisions of Article 143 of the BNS, which pertains to "Kidnapping from India" and Article 144, which pertains to "Kidnapping from lawful guardianship".

Additionally, we request guidance on the procedure to be followed in such cases, as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Article 21(2), which pertains to "Powers to make an arrest without a warrant" and Article 25(1), which pertains to "Procedure for investigation".

Lastly, we seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence in such cases, as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 12(1), which pertains to "Relevancy of facts" and Article 16(2), which pertains to "Admissibility of electronic evidence".

case_description: A factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to BNS, 2023, Section 316, "Trafficking of Persons" - The following query is submitted:

Can a person be held liable under BNS, 2023, Section 316 for allegedly inducing migrant workers to travel from Bihar to their place of employment with false promises, and subsequently, detaining them against their will in locked conditions without providing them with remuneration as per the terms of their employment?

Further, under BNSS, 2023, Articles 73 and 76, "Police Inquiries" and "Magistrate's Power to Investigate", what procedural steps can be initiated by the authorities to investigate this incident and provide relief to the affected migrant workers?

Lastly, can the testimony of the migrant workers be treated as primary evidence under BSA, 2023, Article 27, "Relevancy of Evidence", considering their personal knowledge of the events and circumstances surrounding their detention and non-payment of wages?

case_description: A man kidnapped his ex-wife's 6-year-old child from her home and fled to a different state.
rephrased_query:
Case Reference: Incident of Unlawful Custody and Interstate Abduction.

Query:

Pursuant to Article 321 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of the man, who forcibly took his ex-wife's six-year-old child from her residence, constitutes the offence of "Interference with Custody" under Article 217 (1) of the BNS. 

Further, under Article 43 (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what provisions of the law would be applicable in this situation, specifically regarding the man's escape to a different state, and what steps would be taken by the state authorities to locate and recover the child?

Lastly, under Article 25 (2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what would be the admissible evidence in this case, considering the statements of the ex-wife and any other relevant witnesses, and how would the court determine the credibility of these testimonies during the trial?

case_description: Several girls from a village were promised nursing jobs abroad but were taken to a city and forced into the flesh trade.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is sought to be registered under the provisions of Article 279(1)(d) BNS for the offence of "Trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation", punishable under Article 321(4) BNS.

Further, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a First Information Report (FIR) is required to be filed as per Article 10(2) BNSS, specifying the details of the victims, the accused, and the circumstances of the offence.

Additionally, in accordance with Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the burden of proof for the offence under Article 321(4) BNS shall be on the prosecution, and the defence shall be entitled to raise the presumption under Article 45(3) BSA regarding the accused's innocence, unless the prosecution is able to prove the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

case_description: A couple bought a 4-year-old boy from an orphanage caretaker who had no authority to sell children.
rephrased_query:
**Petition for Injunctive Relief and Investigation under Article 320(1)(b) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 34 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

**To the Hon'ble Judicial Magistrate:**

A complaint has been registered against the caretaker of an orphanage for allegedly selling a minor, a 4-year-old boy, to a couple, notwithstanding the caretaker's lack of authority to do so. The complainants request that this Honourable Court:

1. **Issue an interim injunction** under Article 320(1)(b) BNS to restrain the couple from further detaining the minor and to prevent any harm or exploitation of the child.
2. **Initiate an investigation** under Article 34 BNSS to gather evidence regarding the sale of the minor, the caretaker's involvement, and the couple's knowledge and complicity in the transaction.
3. **Order the preservation of evidence**, including but not limited to, the documents related to the sale, the orphanage's records, and any other relevant materials that may be essential for the investigation.

**In accordance with Article 15 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the complainants request that all relevant evidence be collected, examined, and preserved to ensure a fair and impartial investigation**.

**Respectfully submitted,**

[Your Name]
[Your Designation]
[Your Address]
[Your Contact Information]

case_description: Three men on a motorcycle snatched my gold chain while I was walking on the road and one of them showed a knife.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek clarification on the following:

Whether the act of three individuals, collectively riding a motorcycle and committing a theft of my gold chain while I was lawfully walking on a public thoroughfare, constitutes an offence under Article 456, BNS (Theft), considering one of the perpetrators displayed a weapon, specifically a knife, Article 234, BNS (Threat of violence with a deadly weapon), thereby potentially invoking the provisions of Article 456(3), BNS (Enhanced punishment for theft committed under duress or threat).

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I seek guidance on the procedure to be followed in reporting this incident and the subsequent steps to be taken by the authorities in investigating and prosecuting the offenders, specifically with regard to the requirement for a police report under Article 22, BNSS (Duty of the police to receive information of an offence).

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence of the knife displayed by one of the perpetrators, specifically whether such evidence can be considered as a relevant fact under Article 13, BSA (Relevant facts), and whether it can be used to establish the intent and motive of the offenders under Article 25, BSA (Motive and intentions of an accused).

case_description: A gang of seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash.
A local goon demands monthly protection money from shopkeepers in my area and beats those who refuse to pay.
rephrased_query:
Petition for redressal of grievance under Section 294(1), BNS, and invocation of provisions for protection of citizens under Section 43, BNSS.

The facts of the case are as follows: 

In the locality of [insert location], an individual (hereinafter referred to as the 'accused') has been extorting money from shopkeepers under the threat of violence. The accused is alleged to have used physical force (beatings) against those who refused to comply with the demands for protection money.

The petitioners request the authorities to take immediate action against the accused for his alleged commission of the offence under Section 294(1), BNS, and to grant protection to the affected shopkeepers under Section 43, BNSS.

The petitioners also request the authorities to investigate the matter thoroughly and to take necessary steps to ensure that the rights of the citizens are safeguarded under Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution and to prevent any recurrence of such incidents in the future.

The petitioners request the authorities to provide them with a copy of the complaint registered under the BNSS and to inform them of the further course of action to be taken in the matter.

case_description: While returning from an ATM at night, two people held me at gunpoint and took away all my cash and debit card.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 321, Sub-Section (1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit the following formal legal query:

Whether the perpetrators, who allegedly committed the aforesaid offence by holding me at gunpoint and taking away all my cash and debit card, can be charged under Article 456(1)(a) BNS, for the offence of 'Extortion' (as defined under Article 2, Clause (viii) of BNS) punishable under Section 456 of BNS, and whether the said offence can be investigated under Article 12(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), considering the circumstances of the incident.

case_description: A group of dacoits attacked a village, looted houses, and assaulted several villagers causing serious injuries.
offense_category: dacoity with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Sections 396 and 398 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), and Articles 110 and 128 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is respectfully submitted that a group of persons, allegedly dacoits, have committed a dacoity (Article 3, BNS) and assaulted several villagers, causing them serious injuries (Article 319, BNS). The perpetrators have further committed the offence of theft by looting houses in the village (Article 39, BNS). 

Under the provisions of Article 20, BNS, it is pertinent to inquire about the extent of injuries caused to the villagers and whether any of them have succumbed to their injuries.

Additionally, under Article 15, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is pertinent to inquire about the authenticity and admissibility of any statements or evidence collected from the villagers, witnesses, or the perpetrators in relation to the aforementioned incident.

case_description: Someone showed me a knife in a train and forcibly took my laptop bag and wallet.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal legal query:

Under Article 224, Section 1 of BNS, I request an inquiry into the alleged commission of an offence of criminal intimidation and theft, as per Article 226, Section 2 of BNS. The said incident is alleged to have occurred in a public place, specifically a train, wherein the accused person(s) showed a knife and forcibly took my laptop bag and wallet, thereby causing me to apprehend an immediate threat to my life and property.

I request an investigation into this matter under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically under Article 101, Section 3 of BNSS, to determine the extent of the accused person(s) liability for the said offences.

Furthermore, I request that the investigation be conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice, as laid down in Article 201, Section 5 of BNSS, and that all relevant evidence be collected and examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically under Article 121, Section 6 of BSA, to ensure a fair and impartial inquiry into the said incident.

case_description: A person claiming to be a police officer stopped my car, showed a fake ID, and demanded cash to let me go without a 'challan'.
offense_category: extortion by impersonation of public servant
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS): 
Whether the actions of the individual claiming to be a police officer constitute an offence under Article 43 (Impersonation) of the BNS, particularly insofar as the individual displayed a forged official identification and made a demand for pecuniary consideration to refrain from issuing a 'challan' under Article 27 (Offences Relating to Public Servants).

Also, whether the complainant's actions in complying with the demand, or otherwise, may be considered as an offence under Article 45 (Abetment) or Article 47 (Aiding Person Guilty of Offence) of the BNS.

Furthermore, a complaint under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS): 
Whether the complainant's rights under Article 12 (Right to Freedom from Unlawful Arrest and Detention) and Article 13 (Right to Protection from Unlawful Stoppage and Search) of the BNSS were violated by the actions of the individual claiming to be a police officer.

Also, a complaint under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA): 
Whether any evidence, if any, collected by the individual claiming to be a police officer, can be considered admissible under Article 20 (Exclusion of Evidence Obtained Under Certain Circumstances) of the BSA, and what are the implications of such evidence in the event of a trial.

case_description: Armed robbers hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics.
rephrased_query:
Whether the perpetrators of the aforesaid incident can be held liable under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically Article 321 (Robbery) or Article 322 (Dacoity), for the commission of the offence, and whether the perpetrators' actions constitute a cognizable offence under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), thereby warranting their immediate arrest, as per Article 45 of the BNSS. 

Additionally, whether the evidence collected from the scene, including any statements from eyewitnesses and forensic data, can be admitted in court under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), and whether the burden of proof lies with the prosecution or the accused under Article 78 of the BSA.

case_description: My servant stole cash and gold ornaments from my almirah using a duplicate key he had secretly made.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit the following formal complaint:

Is the servant liable to be prosecuted under Section 381(1)(a) of the BNS for the alleged commission of a misdemeanor, wherein he, with the intention of causing harm, dishonestly misappropriated cash and gold ornaments belonging to me by means of a duplicate key illicitly created and used, thereby violating my proprietary rights as the lawful possessor of such property?

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the authorities take cognizance of this incident and initiate a formal investigation in accordance with Chapter VIII of the BNSS to determine the extent of the servant's culpability and to recover the stolen property. 

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence, including the duplicate key and any other related materials, as potential probative proof in establishing the servant's guilt.

case_description: A known criminal gang has been robbing buses on rural roads; they stop the bus, beat passengers, and take all valuables.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we respectfully seek an authoritative interpretation on the culpability of the perpetrators involved in the following incidents:

(a) On various occasions, a known gang of offenders has forcibly stopped buses plying on rural roads, thereby committing the offence of [Section 321 of BNS: Punishment for wrongful restraint] and [Section 345 of BNS: Punishment for wrongful confinement] against the passengers on board.

(b) Upon stopping the buses, the perpetrators have resorted to physical violence against the passengers, thereby committing the offence of [Section 325 of BNS: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt] and [Section 327 of BNS: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt to extort property or a valuable security].

(c) The perpetrators have further committed the offence of [Section 379 of BNS: Theft] by taking all valuables from the passengers, without their consent and against their will.

We seek guidance on the appropriate legal measures to be taken against the perpetrators under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Additionally, we would like to seek an authoritative interpretation on the admissibility of evidence collected from the crime scenes under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with regards to [Article 42 of BSA: Proof of a relevant fact] and [Article 43 of BSA: Proof of circumstances of an exception].

case_description: A real-estate agent collected advance money for a flat that he had already sold to someone else.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request clarification on the following matter:

Whether the actions of the real estate agent constitute an offence under Section 415 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically the act of misappropriating and fraudulently obtaining advance money from an individual, with the intent to defraud, when the real estate agent had already sold the flat to another individual.

Furthermore, under Article 22(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request information on the procedure for registering an FIR and the subsequent steps to be taken by the authorities in investigating this alleged offence.

Lastly, under Article 14(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request guidance on the admissibility of evidence in court, particularly in relation to the real estate agent's bank statements, emails, and other documents that may be considered as proof of the fraudulent transaction.

case_description: An accountant in our company siphoned off funds by creating fake invoices and transferring money to his personal account.
offense_category: criminal breach of trust and falsification of accounts
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 3(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - 'offence of criminal breach of trust', and Section 2(h) of BNS - 'criminal breach of trust', it is alleged that the accountant has committed an offence of misappropriation of company funds. 

Further, under Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), 'theft' is defined as causing someone to lose their property with the intention to permanently deprive them of it. We suspect that the accountant has created fake invoices and transferred money to his own account with the intention to permanently deprive the company of its funds.

In light of this, under Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), 'cognizance of offences by Magistrates', we request that the Magistrate takes cognizance of this offence under Section 20 of the BNSS and directs the investigation to be conducted under Section 30 of the BNSS.

Additionally, under Section 5 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), 'burden of proof', we request that the burden of proof lies with the accused to prove his innocence. 

We request that the Court directs the investigation to gather evidence under Section 15 of the BSA and that the prosecution must establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

case_description: I purchased a used car online; the seller provided forged RC and insurance documents and the car turned out to be stolen.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek a determination on the liability of the seller for the commission of the offence under Article 265 (Fraudulent Misrepresentation) of the BNS, read with Article 268 (Punishment for Cheating) of the BNS, and the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding the procedure for filing a complaint and initiation of investigation, particularly with regard to the powers of the police under Article 145 (Power to Investigate) of the BNSS, in the event that the forged documents were used to deceive me into purchasing a stolen vehicle, and the seller failed to disclose the true ownership and status of the vehicle as required under Article 122 (Dishonest Misrepresentation) of the BNS.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the admissibility of the evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with regard to the burden of proof under Article 35 (Burden of Proof) of the BSA, and the weight to be assigned to the testimony of witnesses and documentary evidence in establishing the fact that the seller knowingly provided false documents and concealed the true status of the vehicle, thus committing the offence under Article 265 (Fraudulent Misrepresentation) of the BNS.

case_description: A courier agent collected valuables for delivery but never delivered them and switched off his phone.
rephrased_query:
Petition for investigation and prosecution under Section Article 124(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), read with Section Article 37(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Whether the courier agent's failure to deliver the valuables and switching off his phone amounts to an offense punishable under BNS, 2023, and if so, whether a complaint should be registered under BNSS, 2023, for the purpose of initiating an investigation into the matter.

Whether the following acts of the courier agent would be considered evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), 2023:

- The courier agent's failure to deliver the valuables as per the agreement;
- The switching off of his phone;
- Any other relevant evidence that may be obtained during the investigation.

Whether the complainant is entitled to compensation or restitution under the provisions of BNS, 2023, or BNSS, 2023, in the event that the courier agent is found guilty of the offense.

case_description: A man called my elderly mother pretending to be a bank officer and got her to share OTP; Rs 2 lakh was withdrawn from her account.
rephrased_query:
PETITION UNDER THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023 (FOR THE OFFENSE OF CHEATING UNDER SECTION 419 OF THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023)

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I submit this petition to seek your intervention in the matter of a fraudulent transaction involving my elderly mother. On a date and time to be specified, an unidentified individual contacted my mother by telephonic communication, falsely representing himself as a bank officer from a reputable financial institution. The said individual requested and obtained a one-time password (OTP) from my mother, who, in reliance on the false representation, voluntarily disclosed the OTP.

Subsequently, an unauthorized transaction was effected, resulting in the withdrawal of a sum of Rs. 2,00,000 (Rupees two lakhs) from my mother's bank account.

I request that you initiate an investigation into this incident and take necessary action to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.

PRAYER: I pray that the Hon'ble Court may take cognizance of this offense and direct the police to investigate this matter under the provisions of Article 154(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and that the perpetrator may be prosecuted for the offense of cheating under Section 419 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

case_description: My business partner secretly transferred company funds to his personal account and denied any knowledge of it.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 3(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Misconduct in Public Office), Article 7(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Criminal Breach of Trust), and Article 5(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Cheating), I pose the following query:

Whether the actions of the business partner, whereby he clandestinely transferred company funds to his personal account and thereafter denied any knowledge thereof, constitute a cognizable offence punishable under the aforesaid provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and if so, what are the corresponding penalties and procedures to be initiated in accordance with Article 22(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (Police Investigation) and Article 30(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (Arrest and Detention). Additionally, under Article 14(3) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (Presumption), whether the business partner's denial of knowledge can be rebutted by the prosecution by invoking the doctrine of "actus reus" and "mens rea" in conjunction with the burden of proof as stipulated in Article 25(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (Presumption of Guilt).

case_description: A fake charity collected donations from the public for flood relief but used all the money for personal expenses.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a query arises as to whether the accused has committed the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property, under the provisions of Section 415 et seq. of BNS, by soliciting donations from the public under the guise of providing flood relief, thereby fraudulently utilizing the collected funds for personal expenses.

Furthermore, under Article 134 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is sought to determine whether the accused can be prosecuted for the offence under Section 415 et seq. of BNS, in light of the provisions of Sections 204 et seq. of BNSS, relating to the investigation and prosecution of fraud cases. Additionally, the admissibility of evidence under the provisions of Section 60 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) is sought to be clarified, specifically with regards to documentary evidence such as receipts, bank statements, and witness statements that may establish the accused's culpability.

case_description: A jeweller replaced my real diamond with a fake one during a repair and returned the fake stone claiming it was mine.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we submit the following complaint:

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

Subject: Alleged Offence under Article 120 (Cheating by Personation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

We, the complainant(s), hereby lodge a written complaint against [Name of the jeweller], alleging that on or about [Date], the accused person, with the intention of deceiving and cheating us, had replaced our genuine diamond with a fake one while it was under the custody of the accused for repair. The accused then returned the fake diamond to us, falsely claiming that it was the original property of ours.

We request that necessary action be taken under Article 120 of the BNS and Article 59 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the registration of an FIR and further investigation into this matter.

Please note that we shall produce the relevant evidence, including but not limited to, the fake diamond, the original diamond, and any other material documents, in support of our complaint, as per the provisions of Article 25 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

We request that the Hon'ble Magistrate take immediate action in this matter and direct the concerned authorities to investigate and prosecute the accused person as per law.

Yours faithfully,
[Complainant's Name]

case_description: I paid a travel agent Rs 3 lakh for a holiday package but no bookings were ever made and he is now unreachable.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 265 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a formal complaint is sought to be filed against the accused travel agent for the alleged commission of the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property under Article 417(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. 

Furthermore, a request is made to invoke the provisions of Article 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to direct the police to take cognizance of the offence and initiate an investigation, as the complainant has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused has committed a cognizable offence under Article 417(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Additionally, it is requested that the police be directed to summon the accused under Article 61(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and to record the statement of the complainant and other relevant witnesses under Article 62(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, a request is made to invoke the provisions of Article 23(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 to direct the police to collect and preserve all relevant documentary evidence, including but not limited to, receipts, emails, and other communication records, related to the alleged offence.

case_description: A builder collected money from twenty buyers for the same ten flats by showing forged allotment letters.
rephrased_query: Whether the actions of the builder, involving the collection of money from twenty buyers for ten flats by furnishing forged allotment letters, constitute an offence under Article 123(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically in relation to cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property, and whether the provisions of Section 45 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 are applicable for registration of an FIR and subsequent investigation, taking into consideration the relevant provisions of Article 98 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 regarding the admissibility of forged documents as evidence.

case_description: A person published a false article in the newspaper accusing me of corruption without any evidence, damaging my reputation.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Section 415 (Punishment for Cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I, [Complainant's Name], being the wronged party, submit this complaint against [Accused's Name], who has committed the following offense:

On or about [Date of Incident], the accused person, with intent to deceive and mislead, published a false article in a newspaper, falsely accusing me of corruption and thereby causing damage to my reputation. This act was committed without any evidence to support the allegations made against me.

I humbly request the Hon'ble Magistrate to register a case against the accused person under Section 415 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and to take necessary action as per the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for the prosecution of the accused person.

**Additional prayers:**

1. To issue a direction to the accused person to remove the defamatory article from the newspaper and to prevent further publication of such false information.
2. To grant me interim protection from any further harassment or intimidation by the accused person or any other person acting in concert with the accused person.
3. To direct the police to conduct a thorough investigation into the matter and to submit a report to the court within a specified time frame.

I hereby declare that the facts stated in this complaint are true to the best of my knowledge and belief. I pray that this Hon'ble Court may grant me justice and protect my rights as guaranteed under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and other relevant laws.

**Signed:**
[Complainant's Signature]
[Complainant's Name]
[Complainant's Address]

case_description: A factory in our residential area releases toxic fumes every night causing breathing problems for all the residents.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint for Violation of Public Nuisance and Negligence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.**

**Pursuant to Article 10 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, we seek an order for the factory to cease operations forthwith due to the contravention of Article 34 which stipulates that no person shall use any premises so as to cause injury or danger to any other person, or to cause undue hardship or inconvenience to the community.**

**It is further prayed that the factory be held liable under Article 62 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for causing harm to the residents through the emission of toxic fumes, and that the factory owner be directed to pay compensation as per the provisions of Article 98 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.**

**We request that the authorities exercise their powers under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to investigate this matter and take appropriate action against the factory owner for his negligence, as per Article 40 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.**

**We pray that the court may also direct the factory owner to take necessary measures to prevent such incidents in the future, in accordance with Article 31 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.**

**In support of this complaint, we request the court to consider the following evidence:**

- Statements of the affected residents, as per Section 13 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023;
- Reports of the air quality monitoring agency, verified as per Section 28 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023;
- Photographs and videos of the factory's emissions, admissible as per Section 35 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

case_description: Someone is running an illegal lottery office in our neighborhood and many people have lost money.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 34(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I hereby submit a formal complaint regarding an alleged contravention of Article 195(1) of BNS, which pertains to the maintenance of public order, and Article 210(1) of BNS, which prohibits the promotion of gambling.

To the competent authorities under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that an expedited inquiry be conducted pursuant to Article 117(1) of BNSS, to investigate the alleged unauthorized operation of an illegal lottery office in our neighborhood, and its resultant impact on the community, causing financial loss to numerous individuals.

In this regard, I seek the assistance of the authorities to invoke the provisions of Article 234(1) of BNS, which empowers them to prohibit and penalize the operation of such lottery offices. Furthermore, under Article 157(1) of BSA, I request that evidence be collected and preserved to establish the culpability of the accused, and to safeguard the rights of the victims.

I humbly request that this matter be expedited and resolved in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

case_description: A person was singing obscene songs and making vulgar gestures in a public park in front of women and children.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 3 (A), Part II of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek to inquire whether the actions of the person in question constitute an offense under Section 294 (A) of the BNS, specifically with regard to the utterance of indecent words or singing obscene songs in a public place, and whether such actions are punishable under Section 294 (B) of the BNS, considering the presence of women and children in the vicinity.

Additionally, under Article 12, Part III of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we seek to determine whether the actions of the person in question fall within the scope of a cognizable offense, and whether the police have the authority to make an immediate arrest under Article 12 (B) of the BNSS, as well as to inquire about the applicability of the provisions of Article 14 (A) of the BNSS, relating to the power of the police to enter and search the premises.

Furthermore, under Article 15, Part IV of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we seek to assess the admissibility of evidence in this matter, specifically with regard to the testimony of the witnesses, including the women and children present in the public park, and whether their statements can be considered as relevant evidence under Section 8 (A) of the BSA.

case_description: My ex-boyfriend shared my private photographs on social media and created a fake profile using my pictures.
rephrased_query: Petition under Section 513 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for breach of confidentiality, coupled with an application under Article 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to protect the petitioner's identity and seek a restraining order against the respondent, in addition to a request under Section 34 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to authenticate the digital evidence (social media screenshots, private photographs, and the fake profile) and establish the respondent's culpability in creating a false representation using the petitioner's likeness.

case_description: A shop is openly selling obscene magazines and DVDs to school children near a school campus.
offense_category: sale of obscene material to children
rephrased_query: Whether the shop owner can be held liable for violating Article 6 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically the provisions relating to obscenity and indecency, considering the proximity of the shop to a school campus and its potential impact on school-going children, as mandated by Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and what evidence can be admissible under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 to establish the shop owner's culpability.

case_description: A man standing on the road deliberately shows obscene images on his phone to women passing by.
rephrased_query: Is the act of a person publicly displaying obscene images on a mobile phone, thereby causing distress to women passing by, a cognizable offence under BNS, 2023, specifically under Article 321 (Obscene acts and songs), punishable under BNS, 2023, and if so, can a police officer, empowered under BNSS, 2023, Section 19 (Power to seize certain documents and other things), seize the mobile phone as evidence under BSA, 2023, Section 43 (Relevancy of certain facts), for the purpose of investigation?

case_description: A woman was raped by a man who broke into her house late at night when she was alone.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is sought to be lodged by the victim against the accused under Article 302 (Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder) and Article 303 (Culpable Homicide) - as yet to be defined - in lieu of the corresponding sections, and Article 315 (Grievous Hurt) and Article 316 (Assault) for the acts of sexual violence committed by the accused, under Article 318 (Unlawful Sexual Content; Rape). Further, an FIR (First Information Report) under Section 154 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) is sought to be registered against the accused, detailing the sequence of events, including the time of the incident, and the nature of the assault committed by the accused when he broke into the complainant's house without lawful authority. The complainant also seeks the preservation of evidence under Article 22 (Preservation of documents) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for the purpose of investigation and trial.

case_description: A college professor asked a female student for sexual favours in exchange for better grades.
offense_category: sexual harassment and abuse of authority
rephrased_query:
**Petition under Section 4(1)(a) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023**

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

A complaint is hereby submitted against a professor, whose identity and designation are not disclosed, for an alleged contravention of Section 4(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The aforesaid professor, who is a faculty member at a college, is alleged to have abused his official position to solicit sexual favours from a female student, identified as [Student's Name], in exchange for academic benefits, specifically better grades.

**Prayer for action:**

The complainant respectfully prays that this Hon'ble Magistrate takes cognizance of the alleged offence under Section 4(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and initiates an investigation under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for the purpose of ascertaining the truth of the allegations and determining whether the accused is guilty of the offence.

**Relevant Statutes:**

- Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023
- Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023
- Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023

case_description: A man has been following a woman from her office to her home daily, sending unwanted gifts, and watching her through binoculars.
rephrased_query:
The complainant seeks an order of protection under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Section 3(1)(g), against the alleged offender, who is accused of committing the offence of stalking and causing harassment as defined under Article 12 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). 

The complainant requests that the court issue a directive under BNSS, Section 13(2), for the collection of evidence, including the seizure of the binoculars, under the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), Article 7(1)(a), to establish the link between the accused and the alleged offences.

case_description: A man grabbed a woman's dupatta and tried to disrobe her in a market while others watched.
rephrased_query:
Complaint for the commission of an offence under BNS Article 349, read with BNS Article 351, and for being a party to an unlawful assembly under BNS Article 141.

Petitioner seeks registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 154 of BNSS, and an injunction to prevent the repetition of such acts, as permitted under Section 102 of BNSS.

Petitioner requests that the accused be required to provide evidence to establish his innocence, as stipulated under Section 18 of BSA, and that the burden of proof be shifted to the accused under Section 16 of BSA.

Petitioner also requests that the proceedings be conducted in accordance with the provisions of BNSS, and that the evidence be recorded and preserved as per the guidelines laid down under Section 28 of BSA.

case_description: A married man had sexual intercourse with his wife during judicial separation against her will.
rephrased_query:
Whether the act of the married man having sexual intercourse with his wife during judicial separation against her will amounts to the offence of rape under Article 321 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, considering the provisions of Article 213 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 and the circumstances of the case, and whether the said act can be considered an aggrieved act under Article 219 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 for the purpose of recording testimony of the victim.

Pursuant to Article 15 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, can the police register an FIR and initiate an inquiry into this incident, considering the rights of the victim and the accused.

case_description: A man secretly installed a hidden camera in the women's changing room of a gym to record videos.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Section 129(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - Unauthorised Recording of Private Acts:

It is alleged that the accused person installed a hidden camera in the women's changing room of a gym, thereby secretly recording private acts of the female patrons, in contravention of Article XXV of the BNS. 

Requesting investigation and prosecution under the relevant provisions of the BNS, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for the commission of the aforementioned offence. 

Please note that the accused person's actions also raise concerns under Section 67(1)(b) of the BNS - Breach of Privacy Rights of Women.

case_description: A man deceived a woman into believing they were lawfully married and cohabited with her for months.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to clarify the applicability of the definition of "cheating" under Article 120(1) of BNS, in conjunction with Section 24(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, to the facts of a case where an individual (Male A) induced a woman (Female B) to believe that they were lawfully married and subsequently cohabited with her for a period of approximately six months, thereby allegedly causing her to suffer harm under Article 123(2) of BNS.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested to determine the procedural framework governing the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 3(3)(a) of BNSS, in the event that Female B reports the alleged deception by Male A to the law enforcement authorities.

Lastly, it is requested to clarify the admissibility of electronic evidence, including digital communications and other records, under Article 45(1)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), in the context of establishing the elements of the alleged offense committed by Male A.

case_description: A man who is already married performed a second marriage with another woman without disclosing his first marriage.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to elucidate the applicability of the provision pertaining to solemnization of a marriage by a person having a subsisting valid marriage, Article 294 of BNS, in the scenario wherein a man, already in a valid marital relationship, enters into a second marriage without divulging the existence of his prior marital bond. Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), please clarify the procedural framework for initiating proceedings against the accused under the aforementioned Article 294 of BNS, specifically with regards to the requirements for registration of the first information report (FIR) and subsequent investigation. Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), please clarify the admissibility of evidence in a prosecution under Article 294 of BNS, in cases where the accused fails to disclose his prior marital relationship, including the burden of proof and the weight to be accorded to circumstantial evidence.

case_description: A woman left her newborn baby in a dustbin near the hospital and disappeared.
rephrased_query: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek an interpretation of the penal consequences under Section 317 of the BNS in relation to a situation where a female parent abandons her newborn child in a public place, specifically a dustbin near a hospital, thereby leaving the child vulnerable to harm and neglect. Furthermore, we request clarification on the application of Section 304-A of the BNS, which pertains to causing death by negligence, in the event the abandoned child succumbs to injuries or illness. Additionally, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we would like to know the procedural steps that law enforcement agencies must follow to investigate the crime and apprehend the female parent, particularly with regard to the Article 10 of the BNSS, which deals with the powers of a police officer to take cognizance of a crime.

case_description: A begging ring operator hired several children aged 7-10 to beg at traffic signals and took all the money they collected.
rephrased_query:
